extracted.intended_audience: corporate sustainability teams, ESG/reporting specialists, compliance officers and financial/reporting teams at EU and non-EU companies preparing for CSRD
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for companies to determine CSRD applicability, required ESG disclosures (per ESRS), timelines, and practical preparation steps (data, governance, assurance, tooling) to achieve compliant sustainability reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current scope criteria (who must report)
rubrics_metrics.description: CSRD reporting requirements apply to: Large EU companies meeting two of the following: >250 employees, >€40M turnover, or >€20M total assets; All listed companies on EU-regulated markets (except microenterprises); Non-EU companies with >€150M revenue in the EU and a significant EU presence. Medium sized enterprises will also be included in future mandatory reporting requirements, with tailored standards being developed for SMEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EU member states transpose CSRD into national law, so implementation and enforcement may vary across member states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Omnibus Directive changes (scope & timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Omnibus proposals (Feb 2025) introduce significant changes: Narrowed scope: From 2026, only companies with >1,000 employees and either >€50M turnover or >€25M in total assets would be required to report. Delayed implementation: 'stop-the-clock' postpones reporting requirements for wave 2 and wave 3 companies by two years (member states must transpose by 31 Dec 2025). Optional Green Taxonomy alignment for companies with turnover under €450M. Sector-specific ESRS postponed. Reduced enforcement: penalties and supplier contract terminations for non-compliance may be optional. Verification level lowered: reasonable assurance requirements delayed; limited assurance remains the interim standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes aim to reduce administrative burdens while preserving core objectives — but require national transposition and therefore could vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who will need to report in 2027 (thresholds for 2027 reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies that cross the reporting thresholds for the first time in 2026 will need to publish initial sustainability reports in 2027. This group includes: Large EU-based companies that exceed the proposed updated thresholds: more than 1,000 employees and €450 million in net turnover; Non-EU companies with annual net turnover of €450 million or more within the EU, if they operate a subsidiary or branch in the region; Companies listed on EU-regulated markets, regardless of where they are headquartered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your organization fits any criteria, begin preparations now even though some technical details are still being finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-EU company scope and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-EU companies will be required to comply with the CSRD from fiscal year 2028, with reports due in 2029. A non-EU company falls under scope if it: Generates >€450M net turnover in the EU and has either an EU branch already subject to CSRD, or an EU subsidiary with >€50M net turnover. Separate ESRS for non-EU companies are expected but not yet published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you're a European branch of a non-EU group, your CSRD compliance in 2026 or 2027 can help your parent company prepare for future requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key dates and rollout timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline highlights: 2014: NFRD introduced; 2022: CSRD adopted to replace and strengthen NFRD; 2023: CSRD officially in force (since Jan 2023); 2024: First fiscal year of enforcement of the CSRD; 2025: First publication of sustainability reports in compliance with the CSRD ('wave 1' companies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rollout is staggered over several years; different 'waves' have different reporting start dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures — general disclosures & sustainability information
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must disclose essential general information and sustainability information as part of their reported information, including business model, key initiatives, ESG policies and practices, risks and opportunities related to sustainability, impacts of business activities on the environment and society, progress toward sustainability targets, and key initiatives and actions taken to address ESG issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosing information on these aspects is required under the CSRD and will be mapped to relevant ESRS requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental aspects to disclose include Scope 1, 2, and 3 GHG emissions; climate-related risks and mitigation plans (including transition plans and sustainability risks); resource usage (energy, water, waste), with a focus on resource use and its impact on the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disclosures should be detailed, verifiable, and aligned with topical ESRS (e.g., climate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Social aspects to disclose include workforce diversity, pay equity, working conditions, human rights and value chain due diligence, and community engagement including identification and management of impacts on consumers and other stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies must report on how their activities affect people and social stakeholders as part of ESRS topical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Governance-related disclosures include board oversight of ESG issues, ethics and anti-corruption measures, and sustainability risk management to provide transparency crucial for investors to assess governance practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance disclosures support investor decision-making and should show structures, responsibilities and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double materiality principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must report based on double materiality, meaning they must disclose: Impact materiality — How the company affects people and the planet; Financial materiality — How ESG issues affect the company’s performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality assessment determines which disclosures under the ESRS are relevant for each company and filters applicable disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESRS structure and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) developed by EFRAG guide CSRD reporting and include: Cross-cutting standards (general principles, strategy, governance), Topical standards (ESG-specific topics like climate, biodiversity, labor), Sector-specific standards (tailored disclosures by industry — postponed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should map their disclosures to cross-cutting and topical ESRS; sector-specific standards are expected later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step: Conduct a double materiality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which ESG topics are material to your company and stakeholders. This filters applicable disclosures and informs all future reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assessment determines which ESRS disclosures apply and should be repeatable and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step: Perform a gap analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare your existing policies and disclosures against the ESRS. Pinpoint where data, governance, or controls fall short.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the gap analysis to prioritize fixes, remediation and to scope data collection and governance changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step: Establish data governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sustainability data is traceable, auditable, and as robust as financial data. Align systems across business units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good data governance includes mapped data flows, controls, provenance, and centralization or federated approaches that enable audit-readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step: Engage internal and external stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborate across functions (finance, HR, procurement) and engage suppliers and partners early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder engagement supports materiality assessment, supplier data collection, and cross-functional buy-in needed for accurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step: Leverage ESG software
rubrics_metrics.description: Use technology to automate data collection, map disclosures, facilitate workflows, and ensure compliance with digital tagging requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software can automate data collection, map internal data to ESRS disclosure requirements, facilitate double materiality assessments and stakeholder input, enable digital tagging for ESEF format, and create audit-ready outputs to support assurance and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step: Prepare for assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin working with assurance providers early to develop validation processes, especially in decentralized organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start assurance readiness early, design validation processes for decentralized data sources, and ensure outputs are audit-ready; note the current interim standard is limited assurance while reasonable assurance is delayed per Omnibus proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step: Align with global frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Align CSRD/ESRS reporting with global frameworks such as GRI, SFDR, and ISSB (IFRS S1/S2) to support global consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping to other frameworks reduces duplication and helps investors and stakeholders compare disclosures across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance and verification level (current and proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification requirements: limited assurance remains the interim standard while reasonable assurance requirements have been delayed under Omnibus proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should plan for eventual higher assurance levels, work with assurance providers now to create audit-ready outputs, and keep track of evolving assurance timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital tagging and ESEF structured reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: CSRD requires structured reporting under the ESEF format and companies should enable digital tagging of disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital tagging is essential for machine-readable, auditable disclosures — ESG software can help implement tagging and produce structured outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and penalties (implementation variability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Omnibus proposals indicate reduced enforcement options: penalties and supplier contract terminations for non-compliance may be made optional, with the EU Commission overseeing enforcement and sanctions across member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National transposition may lead to variation in enforcement and penalties; companies must monitor national law implementations.
